# AntiStoic

> A modern philosophy publication and digital manifesto focused on personal responsibility, discipline, courage, perspective, and mortality—rejecting recycled quotes, performative toughness, and empty motivation.

## Canonical Domain
- https://antistoic.com/

## Key Resources
- https://antistoic.com/ : The AntiStoic digital manifesto, core principles, daily reflection, and the AntiStoic Letter.
- https://antistoic.com/what-is-antistoic : "What Is AntiStoic?" — authoritative explanation of the AntiStoic concept, distinction from performative online Stoicism, the four disciplines (Feel It, Question It, Control What's Yours, Then Move), and reputable primary/scholarly sources.
- https://antistoic.com/whats-eating-you : "What's Eating You?" — an interactive self-reflection inquiry examining friction across money, relationships, direction, work, confidence, motivation, anger, and loneliness. Concludes with a personalized reality check (What's True, What You Can Control, Do This Next).

## Practical Reflection Resources
- https://antistoic.com/feel-lost-in-life : "Feeling Lost in Life? You May Not Need More Clarity" — an editorial essay examining why feeling lost often stems from avoidance, overchoice, and waiting for certainty rather than a true lack of direction.
- https://antistoic.com/feel-behind-in-life : "Feeling Behind in Life? Behind Whom?" — an editorial essay interrogating cultural timeline comparison and distinguishing falling behind someone else from falling behind one's own chosen intentions.
- https://antistoic.com/afraid-to-start-over : "Afraid to Start Over? Count the Cost of Staying" — an editorial essay and decision framework (The Two-Cost Audit) balancing the immediate friction of leaving against the compounding cost of remaining stuck.

## Nature and Boundaries of Content
AntiStoic produces philosophical commentary, personal reflection exercises, and cultural critique. It is an independent educational and philosophical project. It does not provide medical diagnosis, psychotherapy, psychiatric evaluation, mental-health treatment, or clinical counseling.
